source.title: Blind Single-Layer Activation Edits Show a Break/Fix Asymmetry in Factual Recall

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some tables are flattened in the web text, but the relevant SAE results are identifiable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses superposition and polysemantic co-activation as context for a feature-interference hypothesis, but its experiments concern factual-error detection and repair. It does not measure neuron-level polysemanticity, feature packing relative to neuron capacity, or the claim versions' other named outcomes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE feature-overlap and CIS results related to its feature-interference hypothesis. These do not measure whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs or test the claim versions. Related SAE findings are recorded under fits_no_version; factual-repair results are left out because they do not bear on the claim.
record.test_reason: The study is about factual-error repair by activation edits. Its SAE work measures a concept-interference score (CIS) and SAE feature-set overlap on the Pythia-6.9B residual stream. It never measures whether individual MLP neurons respond to unrelated inputs, and it does not vary capacity, architecture or training to test the cause of polysemanticity. The authors read post-hoc sparsification as 'consistent with polysemantic co-activation', but that is an interpretation of SAE feature statistics, not a neuron-level result. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The main result is a break/fix asymmetry: single-layer corruption flips 74–100% of correct answers, while blind repair fails, with blind non-gradient methods reaching at most +3 pp net. Oracle edits fix 68–82%, implicating a target-specific direction-selection bottleneck. CIS is a negative side result: a weak L1 signal that vanishes under Top-K, which the authors attribute to polysemantic co-activation in dense L1 SAEs.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies activation edits for factual recall and an SAE-based feature-interference hypothesis; it does not reproduce the original neuron-interpretability method.
record.method_sensitivity: CIS prediction depends on SAE sparsity: the weak L1 signal falls to chance-level with native Top-K SAEs and post-hoc sparsification.

fits_no_version.finding: L1 SAE features overlap heavily (Jaccard 0.269) while Top-K overlap is near zero (0.032). CIS prediction (AUROC 0.58) falls to chance under Top-K or post-hoc sparsification. The authors call this consistent with polysemantic co-activation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In SAE decompositions of LM residual streams, apparent feature co-activation or overlap depends strongly on the SAE sparsity regime (dense L1 vs Top-K).

record.code_released: not stated (the paper says code will be released, but gives no URL)
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 4th Workshop on Towards Knowledgeable Foundation Models (KnowFM 2026)
record.problems: The SAE/CIS findings are specific to one model, benchmark, and SAE setup; CIS prediction is weak and depends on the sparsity regime. These results do not directly measure neuron-level polysemanticity.
record.rows_left_out: Factual-repair interventions, corruption rates, oracle comparisons, and probe results were omitted because they measure factual recall repair or detection, not neuron polysemanticity or the claim versions.

untested.parts: Share of polysemantic MLP neurons by layer; not measured.
Superposition is cited as background only; no test of capacity pressure.
Initialization, regularization or noise as causes; not studied.
Effects of activation function, architecture or regularization on neuron polysemanticity; not studied. SAE sparsity is not a model training choice.
Reinterpretation of canonical polysemantic neurons; not studied.
Neuron-level measurement dependence; not studied. The SAE-sparsity dependence of CIS concerns a different construct.

record.verdict_notes: Classification confirmed as discusses/T6. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Image-classifier neurons and responses to unrelated image inputs.
Polysemanticity rates of MLP neurons in transformer language models across layers.
Whether capacity pressure from representing more features than neurons causes neuron polysemanticity.
Polysemanticity from initialization, regularization, or training noise without capacity pressure.
Changes in neuron polysemanticity across activation functions, architectures, or regularization, and performance costs.
Whether purportedly polysemantic neurons have one shared feature or related jobs.
Whether neuron polysemanticity classification depends on activation range or explanation scoring.

rows.subject: Pythia-6.9B
rows.operation_detail: Measured Concept Interference Score (CIS) as a predictor using L1 SAE features.
rows.note: The authors characterize the signal as weak. This measures a feature-interference score, not neuron polysemanticity.
rows.check: CIS AUROC for hallucination prediction; not a neuron polysemanticity measure. The state 'observed' only refers to the weak signal relative to chance.

rows.subject: Pythia-6.9B
rows.operation_detail: Measured CIS prediction with Top-K SAEs.
rows.note: The text describes these results as non-predictive and consistent with chance.
rows.check: Top-K CIS AUROC near chance; this bears on the CIS method, not on any version.

rows.subject: Pythia-6.9B
rows.operation_detail: Post-hoc sparsified the same L1 SAE and recomputed CIS AUROC.

conditions.value: same L1 SAE, retaining top k activations

rows.baseline: Full L1 SAE: .606 in this post-hoc experiment
rows.note: The text says the post-hoc sparsification result matches the native Top-K result. The full-L1 value is .606 here because this experiment recomputes CIS with uniform aggregation; the headline result is .583.
rows.check: Post-hoc sparsification of CIS; the authors' polysemanticity reading concerns SAE features, not neurons.

rows.subject: Pythia-6.9B
rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise overlap between SAE feature sets.
rows.measure: Mean feature-set Jaccard overlap; share of pairs above 0.3
rows.note: The paper reports this as overlap among SAE features, not as a count or rate of polysemantic neurons.
rows.check: Jaccard overlap of L1 SAE feature sets on the residual stream, not MLP neurons. There is no baseline for what counts as polysemantic.

rows.subject: Pythia-6.9B
rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise overlap between SAE feature sets.
rows.note: The text describes Top-K feature overlap as near-zero.
rows.check: Top-K SAE overlap of 0.032, used as a comparator. It reflects the SAE sparsity regime, not neuron polysemanticity.
